messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type:
• 55 mph on rural interstates,
• 65 mph on urban interstates,
• 45 mph on rural highways,
• 35 mph on urban highways,
• 25 mph in school zones (unless posted otherwise). | Speed limits are posted on signs; drivers must obey them. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children under 4 must be in a rear‑facing seat. | Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations carry a $50 fine and points on the driver’s record. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas has a zero‑tolerance policy for drivers under 21. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | Failure to yield can lead to citations and points. | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Stopping distance: 20 ft for 2‑lane roads, 30 ft for 3‑lane roads. | Violations can result in a $50 fine and points. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Drivers must signal before changing lanes.
• Passing on the right is prohibited unless the driver is turning left. | Improper lane changes can lead to citations. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk or intersection.
• No parking in front of a driveway.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is illegal. | Violations may result in towing and fines. | | **Traffic Signal Compliance** | • Red lights mean stop; green means go; yellow means prepare to stop.
• Stop signs must be fully stopped. | Running red lights can lead to a $200 fine and points. | | **Points System** | • Points are added to a driver’s record for violations.
• 4 points in 12 months can lead to license suspension. | Points are tracked by the Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS). | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury, $25,000 for property damage. | Failure to maintain insurance can result in license suspension. | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Trucks over 10,000 lb must have a commercial driver’s license (CDL).
• Bicyclists must obey traffic signals and ride in the direction of traffic. | Commercial vehicles have additional regulations. | ### How to Stay Updated - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** website: [https://www.dps.texas.gov](https://www.dps.texas.gov) - **Texas Transportation Code** (available online) for detailed statutes. - Local county or city ordinances may add additional rules (e.g., specific speed limits or parking restrictions). Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to handle a particular situation!
